```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 90)
# The evaluated examples run against a local replay of responses recorded from
# the production API (tests/testthat/fixtures/recorded, tools/record_fixtures.R):
# no network and no login at build time; the outputs are real API outputs.
soil <- soilhub:::replay_session()
```

```{r}
library(soilhub)
```

This guide explains the two **views** of the data: `view = "raw"` and
`view = "revised"`. It assumes you have signed in as shown in
`vignette("soilhub", package = "soilhub")` (`soil <- soil_connect()`).
The outputs were recorded from the Global Soil Data Hub API in October 2026.

## The principle

The hub is a **mirror** of the ISRIC databases (WoSIS, WISE, SOTER,
SOTWIS): the values, units and codes are kept **as ISRIC published them**,
including their known defects (an impossible value, a duplicated layer, an
estimate stored as a measurement). This is the **raw** view, the default.

Some defects are documented and have a clear rule. The **revised** view
applies those rules on the server: it hides or flags values and rows, and
tells you, in the answer, which rules it applied and how many values each
one touched. Nothing is changed in the database, and the R package never
corrects a value by itself: it only shows what the server did.

## A raw read

We read the first five horizons of WoSIS around Vancouver (Canada), in the
raw view (the default).

```{r}
vancouver <- c(-123.3, 49.0, -122.9, 49.4)
raw <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver, max_rows = 5)
```

We look at the depths and at the bulk density of the field-moist fine earth:

```{r}
raw[, c("horizon_name", "upper_depth_cm", "lower_depth_cm", "bulk_density_fine_earth_field_moist")]
```

Only the fourth horizon (an organic F layer) has a bulk density: 1.6 kg/dm³.

## The same read, revised

The same selection with `view = "revised"`:

```{r}
revised <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver,
                             view = "revised", max_rows = 5)
```

Is the bulk density column still there?

```{r}
"bulk_density_fine_earth_field_moist" %in% names(revised)
```

No: in the revised view the value 1.6 is hidden, and since no other horizon
of these five has a value, the whole column disappears.

## Which rules were applied?

`soil_revised_rules()` lists the rules applied to your selection:

```{r}
soil_revised_rules(revised)
```

How to read it:

- `id` is the number of the rule (R17);
- `title` says what the rule does: WoSIS bulk densities recorded as a
  "guessed value, expert field estimate" are not measurements, so they are
  excluded;
- `issue` is the issue of the API project where the rule was discussed;
- `effect` is what it did (`values_hidden`: values removed from the answer);
- `n` is how many values it touched.

## Where exactly? The markings

The package collects every marking of the rows in one long table, with
`soil_markings()`. We keep only the markings of the revised view
(`scope` equal to `"hidden_value"`):

```{r}
marks <- soil_markings(revised)
marks[marks$scope == "hidden_value", ]
```

Row 4 of the table, column `bdfifm` (the WoSIS code of this bulk density):
the value `1.60` was hidden by rule R17. The original value stays visible
here, so you always know what was removed.

The raw view already carried the reason. In the markings of the raw table,
the cell has `source_method_kind` "guessed value, expert field estimate", as
recorded by WoSIS:

```{r}
raw_marks <- soil_markings(raw)
raw_marks[raw_marks$marking == "source_method_kind", ]
```

The other markings (`method_facets`) describe the laboratory method of each
value, for example "sieved over 2 mm sieve" or "buffered at 7.0" for the
cation exchange capacity.

## Value flags

Some rules do not hide a value but **flag** it (for example an extreme
value). The flags are in the column `value_flags`, and `soil_flags()` lists
them in a long table:

```{r}
soil_flags(revised)
```

None of these five horizons has a flag: the table is empty.

## Retired rows

When ISRIC removes a profile or a value from a new release, the hub keeps
it and says so: the column `retired_in_release` holds the release in which
the row left the source (`NA` when it is still current).

```{r}
raw$retired_in_release
```

All five horizons are current.

## Counts are over the whole selection

The counts `n` of `soil_revised_rules()` are computed over your **whole
selection**, not only over the rows you read. Here we read five
observations of the SOTER polygons in the long layout (one row per measured
value) and the revised view:

```{r}
soter <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "soter_polygons", layout = "long",
                           view = "revised", max_rows = 5)
soter[, c("horizon_name", "property_code", "value", "unit")]
```

```{r}
soil_revised_rules(soter)
```

Three rules acted on the SOTER polygons (R12 appears twice, once per
effect): for example R12 flagged 92 extreme values and hid 2 impossible
values in the whole dataset, although our five rows show none of them. The
header line also says how big the selection is: 364,051 observations.

## The list of rules

The rules the server knows are listed in its capabilities. This loop prints
the number and the title of each one:

```{r}
rules <- soil_capabilities(soil)$views$revised_rules
for (rule in rules) {
  cat(rule$id, ":", rule$title, "\n")
}
```

The full documentation of each rule is in the
[API documentation](https://soilhub.weatherprogapp.it/docs).

## In short

- Use `view = "raw"` (the default) to work with the data exactly as ISRIC
  published them.
- Use `view = "revised"` to let the server apply the documented rules.
- Always look at `soil_revised_rules()` and, if needed, `soil_markings()`
  to know what changed.

```{r teardown, include = FALSE}
soilhub:::replay_stop(soil)
```
